package_info.package_manager: Custom/Unknown (malware toolkit, not public package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (custom threat toolkit, not versioned in public repositories)
package_info.why_malicious: PIPEDREAM is a custom-built malware framework attributed to state-sponsored threat actors, specifically designed to target and compromise industrial control systems (ICS) and SCADA environments. It enables attackers to scan for, exploit, and control Schneider Electric and Omron PLCs as well as OPC UA servers, facilitating privilege escalation, lateral movement, and the disruption or manipulation of critical industrial processes. Its capabilities represent a direct and severe threat to critical infrastructure operations.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (post-compromise, after initial access to OT network)
execution_context.file_location: Custom malware binary deployed on compromised Windows systems (potentially via driver exploitation)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Custom toolset enabling scanning for, compromising, and controlling Schneider Electric and Omron PLCs, as well as OPC UA servers. (No direct code provided in report.)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware scans the OT network for Schneider Electric PLCs, Omron Sysmac NEX PLCs, and OPC UA servers, attempts to compromise them using protocol-specific exploits or default credentials, and issues unauthorized control commands to manipulate or disrupt device operations.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is engineered to automatically discover, compromise, and control critical ICS/SCADA devices, which is highly abnormal and dangerous in any OT environment. Such actions enable attackers to manipulate or disrupt industrial processes without authorization.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate OT software should only interact with ICS/SCADA devices under explicit operator control, with strong authentication, and with comprehensive audit logging. Automated, unauthorized scanning and control of devices is never acceptable.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate device management or asset inventory tools may scan for devices, but only with explicit operator initiation, robust authentication, and detailed audit trails. They do not attempt to compromise or control devices without authorization.
key_indicators: Automated network scanning for Schneider Electric and Omron PLCs, and OPC UA servers
Issuance of unauthorized device control commands to PLCs
Use of industrial protocols (Modbus, OPC UA, CoDeSys) from non-standard or IT-originating hosts
Attempts to authenticate using default or weak credentials
Protocol-specific exploit attempts targeting ICS/SCADA devices

execution_context.file_location: Windows system driver layer (via exploitation of CVE-2020-15368 on ASRock motherboards)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious code exploiting CVE-2020-15368 to gain privileged access on Windows systems with ASRock motherboards, enabling lateral movement into OT/IT environments. (No direct code provided in report.)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At exploit-time, the code abuses a vulnerable ASRock driver (CVE-2020-15368) to escalate privileges to SYSTEM/kernel level on Windows systems, deploys malicious payloads, and establishes persistence to enable lateral movement into OT and IT networks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exploiting a known driver vulnerability to gain kernel-level access is a hallmark of advanced persistent threat activity and is never legitimate in production environments. This enables attackers to bypass security controls, deploy further payloads, and maintain stealthy persistence.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal drivers should not be exploited to execute arbitrary code, escalate privileges, or facilitate lateral movement. Legitimate software should not attempt to load unsigned or suspicious drivers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security researchers may exploit such vulnerabilities in isolated, controlled environments for vulnerability assessment or red teaming, but never in production or without explicit authorization.
key_indicators: Deployment of unsigned or suspicious drivers on Windows systems
Privilege escalation to SYSTEM or kernel level
Creation of persistence mechanisms at the driver or kernel layer
Unusual driver activity or modification of driver files

attack_chain.action: Initial access to Windows systems via exploitation of CVE-2020-15368 on ASRock motherboards.
attack_chain.leads_to: Privilege escalation and deployment of malware payloads.

attack_chain.action: Privilege escalation and establishment of persistence on compromised Windows systems.
Lateral movement from IT to OT networks, targeting ICS/SCADA devices.
attack_chain.leads_to: Discovery and targeting of industrial devices.

attack_chain.action: Scanning for, compromising, and controlling Schneider Electric and Omron PLCs, and OPC UA servers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Disruption or manipulation of industrial processes (final goal).

behavioral_signatures: Automated network scanning for ICS/SCADA devices, specifically Schneider Electric PLCs, Omron PLCs, and OPC UA servers, originating from IT or non-standard hosts
Issuance of unauthorized or unexpected device control commands to PLCs
Exploitation attempts against CVE-2020-15368 (ASRock driver vulnerability) on Windows systems
Deployment or loading of unsigned or suspicious drivers on Windows hosts
Lateral movement activity from IT to OT network segments, especially involving new or unknown hosts
file_indicators: Presence of unsigned or suspicious drivers on Windows systems, particularly on ASRock motherboards
Unknown binaries or services running with SYSTEM or kernel-level privileges
Unexpected configuration changes or firmware updates on PLCs or OPC UA servers
Creation or modification of driver files outside of normal update cycles
network_indicators: Unusual or unauthorized traffic to ICS/SCADA device IP ranges from IT or non-OT systems
Use of industrial protocols (Modbus, OPC UA, CoDeSys) from non-standard hosts or at abnormal times
Outbound connections from OT networks to external or unrecognized IP addresses
Repeated failed authentication attempts to PLCs or OPC UA servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor Windows systems, especially those with ASRock motherboards, for exploitation attempts against CVE-2020-15368 and the presence of unsigned or suspicious drivers. Detect automated network scanning and unauthorized device control commands targeting ICS/SCADA devices by inspecting network traffic for industrial protocol usage from non-standard hosts. Correlate privilege escalation events, new SYSTEM-level processes, and lateral movement from IT to OT networks. Monitor for unexpected configuration changes or firmware updates on PLCs and OPC UA servers, and investigate any outbound connections from OT networks to unknown destinations. Combine these indicators to identify coordinated malicious activity consistent with PIPEDREAM/INCONTROLLER operations.
